content.title: Walkthroughs: checked, guided stories of a PR stack
content.intent: This stack adds Walkthroughs so that a reviewer can read one checked story of a PR stack instead of every diff, started from the dashboard.

chapters.label: Why Walkthroughs
chapters.caption: Reviewing a stack meant reading every diff cold; this stack lets a person ask Junior for one checked story instead.
chapters.body: Before this stack, a reviewer of a PR stack read every diff with nothing to say what each part is for or where the risk is. Now a person clicks in the dashboard, Junior runs a hidden Turn with the walkthrough skill, and the model submits a story whose every citation Junior checks again. Map: #3087 defines the document and its checker, #3088 lets plugins read stacks and diffs, #3090 stores versions, #3124 adds the submit tool and its Turn behavior, #3133 wires the API behind the `walkthroughs` experiment. Review risk sits in repository access and stuck versions.
asks: Is this on for anyone yet?

chapters.label: Citations Junior can check
chapters.caption: The model cites line ranges and messages; Junior copies the code itself and rejects citations that do not resolve.
chapters.body: A Walkthrough is stored as a document: the model's story plus parts Junior fills in. The model cites code by PR, file, side, and line range, and never copies it [1]; Junior copies the cited lines from the provider diff [2]. Before storing, a checker rejects ranges outside a hunk or past the end of the head file [3], and any non-mechanical hunk that no chapter cites. Lockfiles, generated paths, pure renames, and whitespace-only files never reach the model [4].

decisions.claim: Drizzle migration snapshots can reach the model as ordinary changed files.
decisions.concern: The 4,652-line 0101_snapshot.json in #3090 matches no skip rule, so it costs tokens and forces a not-covered entry.

asks: Why is coverage checked per hunk, not per file?

chapters.label: Plugins read code changes
chapters.caption: Core reads stacks, diffs, and files only through a plugin hook, using Junior's system identity.
chapters.body: Core never calls GitHub itself. A plugin implements three reads: the stack, the diff between two commits, and one file at a commit [1]. Core finds the plugin by provider name and calls it with system egress that never uses a person's credentials or asks anyone to authorize [2]. The GitHub plugin asks the Stacks API first, falls back to walking base branches, and keeps only open layers plus the requested one [3]. The walk stops where a branch has two parents or two children [4].

decisions.claim: Merged or closed layers can drop out of a Walkthrough, except the layer that was requested.
decisions.concern: A half-merged stack gets a story that skips the merged base, though the open layers build on it.

asks: Does the diff use the merge base or the base tip?

chapters.label: One version per snapshot
chapters.caption: A new table keeps one live version per stack at its commits, so a second click joins the first.
chapters.body: Each generation is a row in a new table; the document itself goes to object storage [1]. A snapshot key hashes each layer's number, base, and head, and a partial unique index skips failed rows, so an insert either starts a version or returns the live one (`startWalkthroughVersion`) [2]. The migration only creates a table and three indexes, so it is safe to run, and rollback is dropping the table. Conversation lists hide each generation Conversation with a subquery on that table [3].

decisions.claim: A NOT EXISTS subquery in every Conversation list stays cheap because the lookup column has a unique index.
decisions.concern: Lists that scan many Conversations now run the subquery per row, and the stack adds no query-plan check.

asks: Can a failed version be retried on the same commits?

chapters.label: A Turn that can only submit
chapters.caption: A generation Turn gets the submit tool, no way to reach people, and tighter limits than a normal Turn.
chapters.body: A Turn is a generation Turn when its run carries the version it generates, and that flag wins over the Conversation kind [1]. The behavior turns off agents, the review desk, subscriptions, and no-reply; the submit tool exists only when the run carries a version [2]. #3133 adds limits of 80 tool calls and $5 to this behavior [3], which the agent loop uses in place of the app defaults [4].

decisions.claim: A run flag, not a Conversation kind, is enough to select the generation behavior for now.
decisions.concern: A later Turn on that public Conversation, such as a person's reply after the version fails, runs as a root Turn with every tool.

asks: Are 80 tool calls enough for a ten-layer stack?

chapters.label: Submit re-reads every fact
chapters.caption: The submit tool trusts nothing from the sandbox: it re-reads diffs, files, and messages before it stores a document.
chapters.body: The model works in a sandbox that Junior does not trust, so the submit tool loads each layer's diff from the plugin at the recorded commits, once per Turn [1]. It reads head files for citations outside the diff, and copies cited messages only after an access check on the source Conversation [2]. Problems go back as a tool input error, so the model fixes them and calls again [3]. The document is stored, and the row marked ready, only while the version is still generating [4].
asks: Which links may a Walkthrough cite?

chapters.label: Starting and ending a run
chapters.caption: A click claims the version before its Conversation exists, and the end of the Turn fails a version that never submitted.
chapters.body: The start reads the stack, looks for a public source Conversation in the footer marker Junior writes on its PRs, and claims the version with a Conversation id made up front; only the click that started it enqueues the Turn [1]. The Turn worker looks the version up by Conversation id and passes it to the run [2]. When the run completes, `finish` fails the version if it is still generating [3]. A crash skips that step, so a later click fails versions older than 30 minutes [4].

decisions.claim: A Turn that throws can leave its version generating until a click at least 30 minutes later fails it.
decisions.concern: The dashboard shows generating for that time, and clicks on the same commits join the dead version instead of retrying.

asks: What if the source Conversation is private?

chapters.label: Who can start and read
chapters.caption: The routes check the experiment and the source Conversation, but not the viewer's access to the repository.
chapters.body: Both routes return 404 unless the `walkthroughs` experiment is on, and any signed-in viewer can then start a Walkthrough of any repository and PR number [1]. Reads use Junior's system identity, not the viewer's [2]. The only access check is on the source Conversation: a document quotes it, so start and read hide the Walkthrough when the viewer cannot see it, even if it turned private later [3].

decisions.claim: Any signed-in viewer may generate and read a Walkthrough of any repository that the GitHub App can read.
decisions.concern: Excerpts of private repositories can reach viewers without repository access, and each new snapshot can spend up to $5.

asks: Can a viewer read a version by id alone?

chapters.label: How we know it works
chapters.caption: Unit and integration tests cover the checker, the GitHub stack walk, the submit tool, and the start-and-fail lifecycle.
chapters.body: The checker reports a hunk that no chapter cites [1]. The base-branch walk stops at a fork and returns layers bottom first [2]. Through the real tool factory, a citation outside the hunk is rejected and the row stays generating; a good submission then stores excerpts, the lockfile count, and the cited message [3]. The API test shows one Turn per snapshot, a hidden Conversation, and a fresh version after `finish` fails one [4]. This Walkthrough read the tests; it did not run them or read CI.
asks: Is there a test for a Turn that throws?

chapters.label: What to watch after it ships
chapters.caption: Stuck rows, failed submissions, and limit errors show whether generation works.
chapters.body: Watch the version table. A row in `generating` older than 30 minutes is a dead Turn that nobody retried, since the sweep runs only on a click [1]. A high share of `failed` rows with the reason "The Turn ended without a Walkthrough." means the model is not getting through the submit tool [2]. Generations that hit 80 tool calls or $5 raise the limit errors, and a cost near $5 on the read route is the early warning [3].
